Our theoretical predictions show that lighter scalar-field masses produce increasingly strong scale-dependent suppression of matter fluctuations and more pronounced modifications to the CMB temperature power spectrum, whereas heavier masses progressively approach the cold dark matter limit. For the SFDM mass, we obtain a one-sided 95\% lower limit of $\log_{10}(m_\phi/{\rm eV})>-24.04$ from our main joint analysis. We find that replacing the standard cold dark matter fluid with SFDM does not qualitatively alter the constraints on dynamical dark energy or the evidence for its evolution, including a phantom crossing at low redshifts.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.33444.title: Accurate pulsar timing array likelihoods: better low-rank covariance for gravitational wave background
arxiv.org/abs/2610.33444.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.33444v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: In pulsar timing array analyses, the stochastic process describing the gravitational wave background is typically modeled using a Fourier basis at discrete frequencies with an interval $\sim 0.1~\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, with a diagonal Fourier-domain covariance determined by the power spectral density at the corresponding frequencies. Although this rank-reduced modeling significantly accelerates likelihood evaluation and provides a good approximation in many scenarios, it can lead to biased parameter inference because it is insensitive to spectral features on scales smaller than $\sim 0.1~\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. We introduce a better construction of the low-rank covariance for low-frequency processes by maximizing the log-likelihood averaged over an ensemble of realizations drawn from the true model likelihood. In this approach, the basis-domain covariance matrix is sensitive to the entire model spectrum and is generally non-diagonal. Using two mock datasets, we demonstrate improved likelihood accuracy and more faithful recovery of spectral features compared to the conventional Fourier-diagonal model. Benchmark tests show that this new model requires a computational cost comparable to that of the conventional approach.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.33549.title: Catastrophe Structure and Stability of Axion Stars
arxiv.org/abs/2610.33549.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.33549v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Axion stars are self-gravitating Bose--Einstein condensates of QCD axions or axion-like particles. Their stability determines whether they can survive as dark-matter structures and what astrophysical signatures they may produce. Here we combine a non-relativistic Schr\"odinger--Poisson description with catastrophe theory to develop a unified picture of axion-star stability. Beginning with the Einstein--Klein--Gordon system for a periodic axion potential, we derive the effective equations of motion and conserved quantities and construct a one-parameter family of star-like solutions. A Gaussian variational ansatz reduces the problem to an analytic energy functional $E(R;N)$. Within this model, equilibria appear and disappear through Arnold $A_2$, $A_3$, and $A_4$ catastrophes as the particle number $N$ and interaction strengths vary. A repulsive sextic interaction produces two stable branches---dilute and dense axion stars---separated by an unstable branch. The same catastrophe criteria apply beyond the sextic truncation: for the full cosine and QCD-corrected potentials, the fold conditions follow from the complete variational energy and can be evaluated numerically. We also separate stability within the collective-coordinate ansatz from full radial perturbative stability and specify the range in which the non-relativistic treatment is reliable. This framework provides a compact classification of axion-star phases and identifies model-dependent critical masses associated with collapse, bosenova-like emission, and black-hole formation.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.33563.title: Triple Decomposition of Field Gradient Tensors in Space Plasmas
arxiv.org/abs/2610.33563.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.33563v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Characterizing local topology in magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence is fundamental to understanding energy dissipation, intermittency, and coherent structures in space plasmas. Classical double decomposition of velocity ($A_{ij}$) and magnetic ($Z_{ij}$) field gradient tensors into symmetric strain and anti-symmetric rotation components conflates rigid-body rotation with planar sliding shear. Here, we extend the real-Schur-based Triple Decomposition framework to MHD flows, rigorously isolating irrotational normal strain ($N, M$), residual pure shear ($H, K$), and true rigid-body rotation ($R, B$). Applying this method to high-resolution NASA-MMS multi-spacecraft observations in the solar wind and Earth's magnetosheath reveals distinct topological signatures. Solar wind dynamics are predominantly strain-dominated due to spherical radial expansion, whereas magnetosheath turbulence is overwhelmingly shear-dominated, driven by boundary interactions. Crucially, cross-term contributions ($2RH$ and $2KB$) are suppressed to $\le 7\%$ across both plasma regimes, contrasting sharply with neutral fluid turbulence ($\sim 13\%$). This suppression is driven by background magnetic-field-induced anisotropy ($k_\perp \gg k_\parallel$), which confines shearing motions perpendicular to the primary rotation axes. By cleanly separating genuine vortex cores from current sheets and shear layers, the Triple Decomposition provides an objective framework for characterizing plasma turbulence and analyzing data from future multi-spacecraft missions.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.33729.title: Exploring the Limits: Neutrino Mass and Interacting Dark Sector in the DESI Era
arxiv.org/abs/2610.33729.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.33729v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We constrain three interacting dark matter--dark energy scenarios using cosmic microwave background measurements, DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations, and the PantheonPlus, Union3, and DES-Dovekie Type Ia supernova compilations. We consider interacting vacuum energy and interacting dark energy with a constant equation of state in the phantom and quintessence regimes, analyzing each scenario with either a fixed total neutrino mass or a freely varying effective neutrino mass. When the positivity prior is relaxed, all three scenarios favor negative effective neutrino masses for every dataset combination. Although some combinations permit small positive masses, none of the 95\% confidence intervals reaches the minimum mass required by neutrino oscillation experiments. Allowing the effective neutrino mass to vary produces significances for a nonzero coupling reaching approximately $3\sigma$, but the preferred masses remain negative. These results demonstrate that the interaction and constant dark energy equations of state considered here fail to resolve the DESI neutrino-mass tension.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.33759.title: Development of an FPGA-Based Readout System and Functional Characterization of a Custom NSX1 ASIC for X-ray instrumentation
arxiv.org/abs/2610.33759.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.33759v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We developed an FPGA-based readout system for a front-end ASIC (NSX1) with 64 channels to read out a large- area silicon drift detector used in X-ray detection instruments such as the Wide Field Monitor module for the STROBE-X mission concept. The FPGA acts as a central controller for the NSX1 configuration, implementing trigger handling and event sequencing, precise event timestamping, control of an external ADC for digitization, and data transfer to the host PC. The system enables comprehensive ASIC characterization; here, we demonstrate preliminary ASIC functionality and characterization tests using a calibrated pulser for two programmable linear gain responses of 375 mV/fC and 750 mV/fC. These preliminary results validate the low-noise performance of the NSX1 ASIC and demonstrate successful integration of the DAQ system.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.34019.title: Comment on "Effect of perfect fluid dark matter..." [Phys. Dark Univ. 34 (2021) 100891]
arxiv.org/abs/2610.34019.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.34019v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: This Comment clarifies the physical interpretation of the black hole spacetime metric employed by Shaymatov \textit{et al.} [Phys. Dark Univ. 34 (2021) 100891]. We point out that the metric, originally derived in Li and Yang (2012), describes a specific dual-component system consisting of cold dark matter and a phantom field background. Treating this geometry as a single-component ``Perfect Fluid Dark Matter'' (PFDM) with a total equation of state $w_{\mathrm{total}} = -1$ is physically incompatible with the gravitational attraction required for dark matter halos. Furthermore, we clarify the distinct parameter regimes of the original model to prevent potential misapplications in extreme astrophysical scenarios.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.34057.title: Identification of rippling interface between laser-ablated plasma and ambient uniform plasma at rest
arxiv.org/abs/2610.34057.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.34057v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We present laboratory experiments on the early stage of the formation process of quasi-perpendicular supercritical magnetized collisionless shocks using laser-produced plasmas in an ambient uniform nitrogen (N) gas with 1~Torr under the external magnetic field with controlled polarity. An expanding aluminum (Al) piston plasma arising from laser irradiation interacts with a magnetized ambient N plasma, producing a bright, asymmetric self-emission whose global morphology reverses with the magnetic-field polarity. Two-dimensional ideal-magnetohydrodynamics simulations reproduce the main features of the observed structures and indicate that the ripple formation is unlikely to be driven by the Kelvin--Helmholtz instability, but is instead associated with vortex formation at the rounded leading edge of the piston plasma. We show that the bright, rippling emission delineates the Al-N interface, whose intrinsic width is consistent with an electron kinetic scale, and that its upstream side is predominantly composed of N plasma. This identification allows the formation of a supercritical collisionless shock in the magnetized N plasma to be discussed with minimal Al contamination.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.34058.title: Experimental Evidence for Reflected Ions and Ion Temperature Anisotropy in a Forming Supercritical Magnetized Collisionless Shock
arxiv.org/abs/2610.34058.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.34058v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Supercritical magnetized collisionless shocks require ion reflection for dissipation, yet its role during formation remains unclear. Using high-power lasers, self-emission imaging, and collective Thomson scattering, we investigate a forming quasi-perpendicular shock. An upstream emission tail is consistent with a foot-like structure, while ion heating and temperature anisotropy extend upstream of a ramp-like region. These observations provide evidence of reflected-ion-related heating during early shock formation, although the incident and reflected ion populations are not separately resolved. Future measurements of ion distributions and plasma waves could clarify how this heating mediates shock dissipation and particle energization.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.34178.title: Temporal rhythms of uncertainty: Evaluating Mars claims in the Australian colonial press
arxiv.org/abs/2610.34178.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.34178v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Favourable oppositions of Mars gave nineteenth-century astronomers recurring opportunities to test claims about the planet, while telegraphic news and newspaper reprinting carried those claims well beyond the professional observatories. Historians have established the importance of these events to the development of mass-media astronomy. Here, I examine a related question in the Australian colonial press: how did the standing of particular claims change as brief reports, local responses and fuller accounts appeared at different times? Drawing on colonial newspaper coverage from 1875 to 1899, I follow episodes surrounding the major Mars oppositions of 1892 and 1894. Reports of observations attributed to "Professor Pickering" in 1892 prompted both rapid circulation and immediate scrutiny. In 1894, a cable about William W. Campbell's spectroscopic work provoked local disagreement before more detailed accounts became available. These sequences show that a Mars opposition concentrated attention without imposing a uniform progression from anticipation to discovery and subsequent caution. Newspapers carried assessments and renewed speculation at the same time. The Australian case extends work on event astronomy by showing how the timing and form of information arriving in a colonial press network affected the public evaluation of astronomical claims.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.34234.title: Probing In-Medium Neutron-to-Dark-Fermion Conversion with Multimessenger Neutron Star Observations
arxiv.org/abs/2610.34234.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.34234v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Neutron stars provide a natural environment for probing in-medium neutron-to-dark-fermion conversion and its impact on the dense-matter equation of state (EOS). We use multimessenger neutron star observations to map excluded and not-excluded regions of dark-sector parameter space for an EOS ensemble within a non-linear $\sigma$--$\omega$--$\rho$ relativistic mean-field (RMF) framework and determine their overlap across the ensemble. We include a fermionic dark component with repulsive self-interactions of strength $G_\chi$. We consider masses $m_\chi$ near the neutron mass and heavier states accessible in neutron star cores at sufficiently large neutron chemical potentials. To reduce sensitivity to the nucleonic EOS within this framework, we scan $m_\chi=939$--$1500$ MeV and $G_\chi=1$--$100$ fm$^2$ across 21 nucleonic EOSs: a main baseline set of 13 EOSs and soft and stiff limiting cases. Stellar sequences are tested against the requirement that the EOS support at least $2M_\odot$ neutron stars, GW170817 tidal-deformability bounds, and NICER mass--radius constraints, considering the Illinois--Maryland and X-PSI/Amsterdam inference sets separately. For the full ensemble of 21 EOSs, both NICER analyses identify similar regions excluded by all EOSs, with approximate minimum--maximum extents of $m_\chi=939$--$1300$ MeV and $G_\chi=1$--$11$ fm$^2$. Unlike the full 21-EOS ensemble, the main baseline set has a common not-excluded region whose extent depends on the NICER analysis. The soft and stiff limiting cases show how these regions shift when the nucleonic EOS predicts a maximum neutron star mass near $2M_\odot$ or large tidal deformabilities. Across these 21 calibrated nucleonic RMF EOSs, weak dark-sector repulsion is robustly disfavored across a broad dark-fermion mass range, while the extent of the remaining not-excluded region depends on the NICER analysis and baryonic EOS stiffness.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.34325.title: Near-exact Upper Confidence Limits for Axion Haloscopes
arxiv.org/abs/2610.34325.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.34325v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: The data acquisition of axion haloscopes commonly implements sequential adaptive frequency scans. We present a method to calculate likelihood-based upper confidence limits on axion-photon coupling under this circumstance. We compare the likelihood-based method conceptually and quantitatively with tailor-made methods, i.e. the one proposed by Brubaker et al. (Geometric) and its upgrade the Bayesian Power-Measured (BPM) framework proposed by Palken et al. We find that the likelihood method yields average upper limits that are significantly more constraining than those obtained from these methods. For example, expected constraints improve by a factor of 1.4 as compared with the current state of the art when applied to projections for the ALPHA Plasma-haloscope. We further clarify the statistical basis for the Geometric and BPM methods. In particular, we point out the correspondence of BPM to e-values, proposed as an alternative to conventional p-values in statistics.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.34380.title: Spiralling into Dark Energy: Axio-Dilaton Attractors in Light of Current Data
arxiv.org/abs/2610.34380.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.34380v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: In string compactifications, dilaton-like moduli always come paired with axions, and the two fields interact through a curved field-space metric. We study the cosmology of such an axio-dilaton system, in which the dilaton rolls down an exponential potential corrected by a polynomial prefactor and couples to a massless axion through the kinetic function $W=e^{-\xi\phi_1/M_p}$. A dynamical systems analysis shows that the late-time attractor follows a non-geodesic trajectory in field space with equation of state $\omega_\phi=(\lambda-2\xi)/(\lambda+2\xi)$, so accelerated expansion is possible for steep potentials provided $\xi\gg\lambda$. No physical fixed point is phantom. A Bayesian analysis with DESI DR2 BAO, binned Pantheon supernovae and Planck 2018 distance priors gives $\lambda\gtrsim7$--$9$ and $\log_{10}\xi\gtrsim2.5$ at 95% confidence, together with a degeneracy between the two parameters. The model is slightly favoured over $\Lambda$CDM by current data, while the different polynomial corrections cannot yet be distinguished. This contribution is based on arXiv:2609.22539.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.34423.title: Constraining Nuclear Matter from Finite Nuclei: the Ab Initio Perspective
arxiv.org/abs/2610.34423.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.34423v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: This review surveys recent developments in ab initio calculations of finite nuclei aimed at constraining the nuclear matter equation of state. Particular emphasis is placed on observables that connect finite-nucleus structure to bulk properties of nuclear matter, including neutron-skin thicknesses, electric dipole polarizabilities, and monopole sum rules. We discuss how neutron skins and dipole polarizabilities provide information on the density dependence of the symmetry energy, while monopole observables constrain the incompressibility of nuclear matter.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.34554.title: LunarRF: A Terrain-Aware Propagation Engine and Pole-Wide 3GPP Surface Coverage Atlas of the Lunar South Pole
arxiv.org/abs/2610.34554.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.34554v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Artemis surface operations will depend on 3GPP cellular links, yet no public product shows where such links are physically possible across the lunar south pole. We present LunarRF, a GPU system for terrain-aware surface coverage, and the pole-wide atlas produced with it. A footprint engine casts 8192 radial profiles from one of 11,827 candidate masts enumerated by stated rules on the orbit-adjusted LOLA elevation model, takes the viewshed, and evaluates ITU-R P.1812 Delta-Bullington propagation on every profile, continuous through the radio horizon. An order-independent resolver merges the footprints per 20 m cell, making the run shardable and resumable. The atlas covers the disc south of 80{\deg}S at 20 m for four SFCG-recommended surface bands and the IM-2 demonstration band, 1.8 to 25.375 GHz, under a stated link budget, storing per cell the best-server power and identity, redundancy count, line of sight and coverability. The engine is validated against a parabolic-equation solver, ray tracing and analytic solutions. Swapping Deygout for Delta-Bullington, or adding terrain noise at the level of the published height-error map of the DEM, moves the coverable class on under 1% of a mast's disc in the mean. With every candidate active, 90.5% of the disc is coverable at 1.8 GHz, 59% at 5.855 GHz and 10% at 25.375 GHz, or 84, 43 and 5% after the measured 3-4 dB engine optimism. A mast covers about 90% of its visible area within its budget-set range, and no band is terrain-limited. The nine current Artemis regions are 85-99% coverable at 1.8 GHz and 22-85% at 5.855 GHz. The atlas and candidate table are released with a DOI.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.35124.title: Relating Dark Dimension Size with Dark Energy via 5D Quintessence Potential and Casimir Energy
arxiv.org/abs/2610.35124.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.35124v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We explore effective field theory (EFT) realizations of the dark dimension (DD) scenario in which the size of the DD is determined by the competition between a 5D quintessence potential and the Casimir energy. When only contributions from massless fields are considered, the Casimir energy does not have a typical energy scale, and the 4D dark energy (DE) scale is set by the height of the 5D quintessence potential. The simple 5D model we first study has an attractive feature that the size of the DD is related to the 4D vacuum energy (VE), as outlined above. However, it turns out that the 4D VE thus obtained cannot work as the 4D DE in the standard cosmological setting. One of the discrepancies between the VE and the DE manifests in the radion dependence of the effective 4D Newton's gravitational constant. This leads us to explore a 5D model in which the 4D Einstein-Hilbert (EH) action is dominantly induced by quantum effects, leaving the radion dependence of the 4D Newton's constant subdominant. This model leads to an attractive cosmological model, realizing the mechanism explained in the beginning. We also explore a 6D model with the total internal volume fixed, to make the 4D Newton's constant independent of the radion. We first study a scenario in which the sizes of the 5th and the 6th dimensions are of the same order. In this scenario, the physical origin of the size of the DD is left to its UV completion. Next, we turn to a scenario in which there is a large hierarchy between the sizes of the 5th and the 6th dimensions. In this scenario, the energy scale of the 5D quintessence potential turns out to be much higher than the energy scale of the 4D DE as inferred from the cosmological observations, so we need to subtract a constant term in 4D to tune the 4D DE. This prevents us from obtaining the scaling relation for the DE expected in the dSDC.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.35156.title: $\Delta(1232)$ isobars and neutrino opacities in hot dense matter
arxiv.org/abs/2610.35156.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.35156v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We calculated the diffusion mean free paths of electron neutrinos and antineutrinos in hot, neutrino-trapped matter containing $\Delta(1232)$ isobars, as found in proto-neutron stars and neutron star merger remnants. We included charged-current absorption with the $N\Delta$ weak vertex of weak pion production, neutral-current scattering on all baryons and three-body antineutrino absorption on electron--baryon pairs, with relativistic mean-field kinematics. The reaction $ ar
u_e+e^-+n	o\Delta^-$ dominates the antineutrino opacity whenever the neutron and electron chemical potentials exceed the in-medium $\Delta^-$ rest energy, even where the $\Delta$ population is negligible. At two to four times saturation density, where the reaction is open, it shortens the antineutrino mean free path from

Because antineutrinos are scarce at high lepton fraction, this changes lepton-number diffusion only at low lepton fraction, by up to \DtwoRedHi\% at these densities and by a factor of \DtwoRedLow\ at 1.5 times saturation density. For electron neutrinos, absorption on the $\Delta^-$ and, at low lepton fraction, the opening of nucleonic absorption shorten the mean free path by factors of up to

arxiv.org/abs/2610.35379.title: Revisiting supernova constraints on dark gauge bosons
arxiv.org/abs/2610.35379.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.35379v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We revisit the supernova constraints on three well-motivated light gauge bosons: the dark photon, the $U(1)_{B-L}$ gauge boson, and the $U(1)_{L_\mu-L_\tau}$ gauge boson. For the dark photon and the $U(1)_{B-L}$ gauge boson, we re-evaluate the nucleon bremsstrahlung process within the one-pion exchange approximation, retaining the full momentum and mass dependence. The geometrical dependence of the decay and absorption of these gauge bosons inside the supernova core is also taken into account. Updated bounds on these models are derived based on the cooling of SN1987A and energy deposition constraints from low-energy supernovae (LESNe). Taking the SFHo-18.8 $18.8\,M_\odot$ profile, the SN1987A cooling constraints reach masses of about $230$ MeV, $280$ MeV, and $300$ MeV for the dark photon, the $U(1)_{B-L}$ boson, and the $U(1)_{L_\mu-L_\tau}$ boson, while the corresponding LESN limits extend to about $450$ MeV, $440$ MeV, and $600$ MeV, respectively. The kinetic mixing parameter $\epsilon$ for dark photon, the gauge coupling $g_{BL}$ in the $U(1)_{B-L}$ model, and the gauge coupling $g_{\mu\tau}$ for the $U(1)_{L_\mu-L_\tau}$ model are constrained down to $5.8\times10^{-12}$, $2.9\times10^{-16}$, and $6.4\times10^{-12}$, respectively.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.35424.title: Nuclear fission: from fundamentals to frontiers
arxiv.org/abs/2610.35424.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.35424v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Nuclear fission, the division of a heavy atomic nucleus into lighter fragments, is a process of fundamental importance to nuclear physics, energy production, and the origin of the elements. This chapter, part of the Encyclopedia of Nuclear Physics, provides a pedagogical introduction to a broad array of topics in fission physics, progressing from the macroscopic liquid-drop model and microscopic shell corrections through fission dynamics, observables, modern theoretical frameworks, and experimental techniques ranging from traditional double-energy methods to inverse kinematics at radioactive-ion-beam facilities. The roles of fission in astrophysical nucleosynthesis, nuclear energy, medical isotope production, and national security are discussed, and open questions including the predictive power of microscopic theory and the fission properties of neutron-rich nuclei relevant to heavy element nucleosynthesis are highlighted.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.35449.title: Parameter-Decoupling-Informed Learning for Superresolution: Laboratory Validation and Galaxy Imaging
arxiv.org/abs/2610.35449.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.35449v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We present a parameter-decoupling-informed learning model for estimating subwavelength separations of point sources, without requiring prior knowledge of source properties, control over the sources, or continued access to their light signals. The method builds on our parameter-decoupled quantum superresolution estimation theory, which circumvents the need to estimate nuisance parameters such as partial coherence, brightness imbalance, and relative phase. Our convolutional neural network further accommodates practical imperfections, including background noise, photon loss, and centroid and orientation misalignment. We validate the method using synthetic and experimentally generated images, achieving separation-estimation fidelity above $82\%$ for separations as small as approximately $0.075\sigma$, where $\sigma$ is the Gaussian intensity-PSF standard deviation. This corresponds to an illustrative separation of $\sim13.5$ nm when $\sigma=180$ nm, suggesting potential relevance to length scales addressed by advanced active-source microscopy. Applied to archival Hubble images of NGC~4486B, the model yields nuclear separations of 9.3-13.2~pc, consistent with the previously reported value of 12~pc. Comparisons using the same training and testing images demonstrate substantially higher fidelity than conventional direct data-driven learning in the tested cases. The method's robustness to varying source properties and imaging imperfections supports retrospective astrophysical image analysis and motivates applications in live-cell microscopy and quantum metrology where source control or renewed optical measurements are impractical.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.35506.title: A living catalog of stream interaction regions in the Parker Solar Probe era
arxiv.org/abs/2610.35506.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.35506v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Stream interaction regions (SIRs) and corotating interaction regions (CIRs) are important phenomena in heliospheric physics. These large-scale structures vary temporally and spatially, both in latitude and with radial distance. The additions of Parker Solar Probe (PSP) and Solar Orbiter have allowed for investigations into the radial evolution of these structures over a wide range of heliocentric distances for the first time since the Helios era. To better enable investigations of SIRs and CIRs within the inner heliosphere, we have developed a living catalog of SIR and CIR observations by Parker Solar Probe with corresponding observations by STEREO-A as well as ACE and Wind at 1 au. The methodology used for the identification of events and the generation of this catalog, the initial catalog of PSP observations spanning orbits one through five along with corresponding 1 au observations, and information on accessing the living catalog for future studies is described. This list of SIR and CIR events from PSP and corresponding observations from other heliophysics missions will enable case studies utilizing unique orbital arrangements, as well as aid in future statistical studies to further understand the properties and evolution of these structures.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.35520.title: Delayed maximum energy solar energetic particle events: Statistical analysis from Solar Orbiter
arxiv.org/abs/2610.35520.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.35520v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Investigations of solar energetic particles (SEPs) have long utilized the dispersive nature of onset times, as in, the earlier arrival of higher-energy particles compared to lower-energy particles, to infer information such as the path length to the acceleration site at the time of initial particle release. However, recent observations by Solar Orbiter and Parker Solar Probe have begun to characterize SEP events with an apparent delay in arrival times of the higher energy portion of the particle distribution, above a critical energy separating the delayed particles from that of the typical velocity dispersion signature at lower energies. Features of these delayed maximum energy (DME) SEP events, sometimes referred to as "inverse velocity dispersion" events, could provide new insight into the impacts of magnetic connectivity to locations along an expanding coronal mass ejection-driven (CME-driven) shock wave, variations of acceleration along the shock surface, and transport effects in the inner heliosphere. This study focuses on the occurrence rate and characteristics of DME events observed by Solar Orbiter relative to their footpoint locations with respect to the initial flare site. These DME events show a bias in occurrence rate towards events when the observer's footpoints were westward of the associated flare location. Additionally, estimated locations at which the highest-energy particles of DME events are released into the flux tube suggest continued release of increasingly higher-energy particles from the CME-driven shock into the connected flux tube well into the inner heliosphere. This indicates that DME events could be attributed to inner heliospheric effects and are not actually coronal in origin. This finding is consistent with previous observations and interpretations of SEP events connected westward of the associated flare.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.35589.title: Gravitationally Induced Polarization-Angle Rotation in Pulsar-Black Hole Binaries
arxiv.org/abs/2610.35589.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.35589v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Radio pulsars emit highly polarized radiation whose polarization properties are commonly described by the Rotating Vector Model (RVM). In this work, we investigate the effects of gravitational light bending and parallel transport on the polarization profile of a pulsar in a hypothetical binary system with a black hole (BH) companion. We combine the RVM with numerical integration of null geodesics to calculate the polarization direction along the photon trajectory and model the orbital-phase-dependent variation of the observed polarization position angle (PPA). We consider both non-spinning and spinning black hole companions and include the evolution of the orbital geometry due to relativistic spin-orbit coupling. For a non-spinning black hole, the change in the observed polarization direction arises from the geometric shift associated with gravitational light bending. For a spinning black hole, frame dragging introduces an additional geometric shift, while parallel transport produces an additional polarization rotation measured relative to our chosen reference construction. We investigate the dependence of these polarization changes on the binary parameters and the orientation of the pulsar spin. We find that gravitational light bending can significantly distort the characteristic S-shaped PPA profile, particularly near superior conjunction, and can reverse its overall sense of variation for the supermassive black hole system considered here. Relativistic spin-orbit evolution also affects the orbital-phase dependence of the polarization profile, particularly in the supermassive black hole system. These results show that relativistic photon propagation can modify both the shape and the phase dependence of pulsar polarization profiles and may provide a useful probe of the geometry of pulsar-BH binaries when such systems are discovered.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.35602.title: Nonlinear Tides of Binary Neutron Stars
arxiv.org/abs/2610.35602.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.35602v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Nonlinear tides couple stellar oscillations and reshape the gravitational wave (GW) signal from inspiralling binaries. We present hydrodynamic simulations of nonlinear tides in inspiralling neutron-star binaries and, within a mode-coupling model, derive a semi-analytic quadrupolar fundamental mode-frequency shift through second order in the tidal strength. The two approaches agree in the perturbative regime, but diverge at stronger tidal fields, where perturbation theory breaks down. In the late inspiral, nonlinear tides reduce the fundamental-mode frequency by ${\sim}10\%$ for equal-mass binaries and add a GW phase shift of $\mathcal{O}(1)$ radian beyond the linear tidal response. These effects make nonlinear tides a promising target for next-generation GW detectors.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.35617.title: Distilling neural networks into equations to predict planetary instability
arxiv.org/abs/2610.35617.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.35617v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: The problem of predicting when a multi-planet system will become dynamically unstable has defied analytical progress over the past three hundred years. Recent machine learning advances achieve high predictive performance of instability dynamics, but as black-box systems cannot be interpreted to connect to existing scientific understanding. Here we show analytic equations that predict when a multi-planet system will undergo instability. We discover these equations by first training a neural network on a dataset of N-body simulations, and then distilling its latent knowledge into closed-form algebraic expressions. Our two-stage pipeline first learns an interpretable variable basis, then searches for equations using symbolic regression. The resulting equations outperform existing analytic estimates of instability and apply across wide ranges of mass ratios, spacing, and orbital eccentricities. They capture structure in the prediction landscape with a small number of variables amenable to dynamical interpretation. These results demonstrate how symbolic learning can be combined with neural networks to extract scientific insight from complex dynamical systems.

arxiv.org/abs/2610.35860.title: Direct measurement of the ${}^{23}\mathrm{Mg}(p, {\gamma}){}^{24}\mathrm{Al}$ reaction using the DRAGON recoil separator and a hybrid array of ${\gamma}$-ray detectors
arxiv.org/abs/2610.35860.excerpt:
arXiv:2610.35860v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Background: The $^{23}$Mg$(p,\gamma)^{24}$Al reaction plays a key role in nova nucleosynthesis, serving as a bridge between the Ne-Na and Mg-Al cycles and impacting synthesis of a wide variety of nuclides. It is crucial that the rate of this reaction be well constrained by experimental data, in particular the properties of the key resonance at $E_{\mathrm{cm}}\approx480$ keV, which dominates the rate at nova temperatures.
  Purpose: Our study aims to improve experimental constraints on the energy and strength of the key $E_{\mathrm{cm}}\approx480$ keV $^{23}$Mg$(p,\gamma)^{24}$Al resonance through a new direct measurement of its strength and energy.
  Methods: We used a $^{23}\mathrm{Mg}$ radioactive beam to directly observe capture into the $E_{\mathrm{cm}}\approx480$ keV resonance in inverse kinematics. The $^{24}\mathrm{Al}$ recoils were selected by the DRAGON recoil separator, and coincident $\gamma$ rays were measured in a hybrid $\mathrm{LaBr}_3/\mathrm{CeBr}_3/\mathrm{BGO}$ scintillator array. The $^{24}\mathrm{Al}$ singles yield was used to determine the resonance strength, while the time difference between the coincident $\gamma$ rays and the incident beam was used to determine the resonance energy.
  Results: We obtained a strength of $\omega\gamma=38(7)$ meV and an energy of $E_{\mathrm{cm}}=478.8(26)$ keV for the key astrophysical $^{23}\mathrm{Mg}(p,\gamma)^{24}\mathrm{Al}$ resonance.
  Conclusions: Our reported strength is in excellent agreement with the previously reported direct measurement, as well as shell model calculations. Our energy is in good agreement with earlier indirect measurements. Reaction rate calculations incorporating our results indicate that the $^{23}\mathrm{Mg}(p,\gamma)^{24}\mathrm{Al}$ rate is constrained to a $1\sigma$ up/down factor of 1.5 or smaller in the nova temperature range of 0.2--0.4 GK.

arxiv.org/abs/2507.07174.title: The Unhurried Universe: A Continued Search for Long Term Variability in ASAS-SN
arxiv.org/abs/2507.07174.excerpt:
arXiv:2507.07174v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We search a sample of 5,685,060 isolated sources in the All Sky Automated Survey for SuperNovae (ASAS-SN) with 14.5<15 mag for slowly varying sources with brightness changes larger than ~0.03 mag/year over 10 years. We find 426 slowly-varying systems. Of these systems, 200 are identified as variables for the first time, 226 are previously classified as variables, and we find equal numbers of sources becoming brighter and fainter. Previously classified systems were mostly identified as semi-regular variables (SR), slow irregular variables (L), or unknown (MISC or VAR), as long time scale variability does not fit into a standard class. Much like Petz & Kochanek 2025, the sources are scattered across the color magnitude diagram and can be placed into 5 groups that exhibit distinct behaviors. There are also six AGN. There are 262 candidates (~62 percent) that also show shorter time scale periodic variability, mostly with periods longer than 10 days. The variability of 66 of these candidates may be related to dust. Combining the new slow variable candidates with the candidates from Petz & Kochanek 2025, we have found a total of 1208 slow variables.

arxiv.org/abs/2509.08044.title: spherical: A Comprehensive Database and Automated Pipeline for VLT/SPHERE High-Contrast Imaging
arxiv.org/abs/2509.08044.excerpt:
arXiv:2509.08044v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: I present spherical (https://github.com/m-samland/spherical), a software package and database for the ESO VLT/SPHERE high-contrast imager. SPHERE has produced the world's largest archive of direct imaging observations of exoplanets, substellar companions, and circumstellar disks, but the archive can only be searched by header keywords, and raw data and calibrations must be retrieved by hand. spherical combines a curated, searchable database of the complete SPHERE observation history with automated reduction pipelines for the Integral Field Spectrograph (IFS) and for IRDIS dual-band imaging (DBI). Observations are cross-matched against SIMBAD, Gaia DR3, and the MOCA database, so samples can be selected by stellar properties, age, and association membership as well as by observing mode and conditions. The August 2026 release, archived on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15147730), covers 2014 May to 2026 August and includes 6101 IRDIS DBI, 4733 IFS, 1205 IRDIS polarimetric, and 355 sparse aperture masking sequences. Each release comes with metadata, such that an analysis can be traced to the exact database state it used. The pipelines download raw data and calibrations from the ESO archive, extract IFS spectral cubes with the adapted open-source CHARIS pipeline, calibrate IRDIS data in a parallel workflow, and post-process both with the TRAP algorithm for companion detection, astrometry, and contrast spectra. The code is written in Python and installs with pip, without ESO pipeline software, and the IRDIS reduction reproduces the published photometry and astrometry of 51 Eridani b. spherical makes it practical to assemble homogeneous samples for population studies and to reprocess the full archive uniformly, and it can also serve as the retrieval and pre-processing stage for community tools such as VIP, pyKLIP, and IRDAP.

arxiv.org/abs/2512.07696.title: ZTF-SEDm Type Ia supernova sample for Twins Embedding spectrophotometric standardization
arxiv.org/abs/2512.07696.excerpt:
arXiv:2512.07696v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: This paper has two aims: the first aim is to build a large homogeneous spectrophotometric sample of Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia), using 3069 spectra from the second data release of the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF DR2). Using this sample we reproduce, as the second objective of the paper, the Twins Embedding (TE) spectrophotometric standardization method, which led to an exceptionally low value of 0.073 mag for the intrinsic scatter. We improved the flux-calibration accuracy of the SEDm SN Ia spectrum sample using the ZTF photometric data, which are calibrated at the percent level. We then applied the three steps of the TE parameterization to a subset of 783 ZTF SN spectra near maximum light, and analyse the resulting standardization methods. The precision of the phase-correction model, which is the first step of the TE, is estimated at 0.01 mag in g band, using ZTF data. Despite the challenge posed by the ZTF spectrum-extraction pipeline, we applied a first standardization in color based on the second step of the TE, called Read Between The Lines (RBTL). When considering the scatter due to redshift error and flux calibration error, we estimated a 0.129 mag Hubble residual scatter for this ZTF sample as an upper limit. As expected from the low spectral quality, the final TE standardization based on three nonlinear parameters did not improve the overall dispersion. We release 1897 flux calibrated spectra of 1607 SNe Ia with an estimated photometric accuracy of 0.07 mag. We further demonstrate the ability to apply a spectrophotometric standardization with limited quality spectra. The RBTL standardisation is more efficient than that of SALT with one less parameter, and the resulting host steps are consistent with zero, making it less prone to astrophysical bias. For future spectroscopic surveys, a better spectral quality would enable the full TE standardization to be computed. (Abridged)

arxiv.org/abs/2512.13038.title: Redshift Classification of Optical Gamma-Ray Bursts using Supervised Learning
arxiv.org/abs/2512.13038.excerpt:
arXiv:2512.13038v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Modern satellite missions localize many gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), but spectroscopic redshifts remain scarce because rapid optical follow-up is often unavailable. Optical plateau classification differs fundamentally from its X-ray counterpart: heterogeneous ground-based follow-up, dust extinction, and chromatic afterglow behavior introduce greater incompleteness than in the X-ray data. We present a supervised machine-learning classification of long-duration GRBs (duration $>$ 2 s) with measured redshifts and possessing optical plateau emission. As predictors, we combine plateau and prompt-emission observables. Using 171 such GRBs, we evaluate binary classification --- whether a GRB is high- or low-$z$ --- at thresholds $z_t = 2.0, 2.5$, and $3.0$. The best classifier, at $z_t = 2.0$, achieves a training-set true positive rate (TPR) of 0.741 and an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.841, with a train-to-test AUC difference within 4 percent. The novelty of this work is a classifier built on an optical-plateau-selected sample. Prompt-emission and absorption variables are favored over plateau parameters at $z_t = 2.0$ on the raw (complete-case) data with the Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO), thus allowing a reliable classifier without waiting for the plateau signatures in the light curve. The X-ray absorption column density, $\log(\mathrm{NH})$, and the prompt-emission peak flux, $\log(\mathrm{PeakFlux})$, are stably selected by both the optical and X-ray classifiers. We publicly release a web-based application for the optical classifier, complementing the available X-ray classifier \citep{dainotti2025grbredshiftclassifierfollowup}, to help the community rapidly select high-$z$ GRBs for follow-up.

arxiv.org/abs/2601.16674.title: Constraining Twin-Star Existence in Four-Parameter Maxwell Equation of State
arxiv.org/abs/2601.16674.excerpt:
arXiv:2601.16674v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Twin stars (TSs) are predicted to exist in nature if the hadron-to-quark phase transition is strong enough to form a new branch of hybrid stars, separated from the branch of neutron stars. It is essential to study the hybrid equation of states (EoSs) that can form TSs, with a primary focus on estimating the onset of the phase transition and its strength. We systematically study the TS scenario by adopting a four-parameter Maxwell-CSS approach to construct a large ensemble of Maxwell-type hybrid EoSs. Within this framework, we report the conditions on our parameter space imposed by the TOV solutions. For a fixed transition energy density and speed of sound for quark matter, we define distinct ranges of transition pressures based on the allowed strengths of discontinuity. Below a maximum transition pressure, a range of discontinuity exists that increases as the transition pressure decreases. Thereby, we identify the loci of the limits on discontinuities as the TS existence boundaries. Based on the causality limit, the TS existence boundaries can be truncated. Strong constraints on this picture are drawn from the CET, GW170817 and NICER. Within our considered model, we computed conditional extrema surviving the adopted $2\sigma$ filters---the maximum mass for TSs to be $2.05~M_\odot$, the allowed strongest discontinuity in rest-mass density to be $7.76\rho_\mathrm{sat}$, and the upper bound on transition rest-mass density to be $4.03\rho_\mathrm{sat}$. Subsequently, we compute the implications of the stiffness of the quark matter EoS on this picture. Different confidence levels for observational constraints are considered to assess the extent to which Maxwell-type EOSs remain compatible with the observations.

arxiv.org/abs/2601.18149.title: JWST Spectroscopic Census of ALMA Faint Submillimeter Galaxies in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field
arxiv.org/abs/2601.18149.excerpt:
arXiv:2601.18149v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present a JWST/NIRSpec rest-frame optical spectroscopic census of ALMA 1-mm continuum sources in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field (UDF) identified by the deep ALMA UDF and ASPECS programs. Our sample is composed of the ALMA flux-limited ($S_{1\,\mathrm{mm}}\gtrsim 0.1\,\mathrm{mJy}$) sources observed with medium-resolution NIRSpec spectroscopy from JADES and SMILES, 16 faint submillimeter galaxies (SMGs) at spectroscopic redshifts of $z\sim 1$-$4$. These SMGs show bright longer-wavelength optical lines (H$\alpha$, [N II]$\lambda\lambda6548,6583$, and [S II]$\lambda\lambda6717,6731$) and faint shorter-wavelength optical lines (H$\beta$ and [O III]$\lambda\lambda4959,5007$) with a large nebular attenuation, $E(B-V)\sim0.3$-$1.8$. We test the SMGs using BPT diagnostics and Chandra X-ray fluxes, and find that most SMGs are classified as AGNs; the AGN fraction is $\sim80\%$ for the SMGs at $M_*>10^{10.5} M_\odot$. We find only one SMG ($<10\%$) with a broad Balmer line, indicating that the SMGs are predominantly obscured AGNs. With the optical lines, we estimate the metallicities of the SMGs to be moderately high, $\sim0.4$-$2 Z_\odot$, exceeding the model-predicted dust-growth critical metallicity ($\sim0.1$-$0.2Z_\odot$), which naturally explains the dusty nature of the SMGs. Interestingly, the SMGs fall in the mass-metallicity relation and the star-formation main sequence, showing no significant differences from other high-$z$ galaxies. Similarly, we find electron densities of $n_e\sim10^2$-$10^3\,\mathrm{cm}^{-3}$ for the SMGs that are comparable with other high-$z$ galaxies. Together with the high SMG fraction ($\sim 100\%$) at the massive end ($M_*>10^{10.5} M_\odot$), these results indicate that the SMGs are mostly not special, but typical massive star-forming galaxies at high redshift.

arxiv.org/abs/2602.23474.title: Transient X-ray Sources as Extremely Eccentric Mass-Transfer Binaries with Compact Companions
arxiv.org/abs/2602.23474.excerpt:
arXiv:2602.23474v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: It has long been suggested that X-ray transients are produced at periastron of stellar-compact object binaries with eccentric orbits. Recoil of matter evaporated from the star by X-rays from matter transferred at periastron increases the orbital semi-major axis and eccentricity. After periastrons the object would be a transient X-ray source, a Galactic analogue of a tidal disruption event (TDE), but recurrent with a gradually increasing period rather than catastrophic.

arxiv.org/abs/2603.02828.title: Diffusive dark fluids with Planck-2018 and DESI BAO DR2 Measurements
arxiv.org/abs/2603.02828.excerpt:
arXiv:2603.02828v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: In this paper, we constrain the diffusive dark fluid cosmological model, wherein energy is transferred between the two dark components through a diffusion process. We extended the work in Ref. \cite{sahlu2026observational} by employing Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) data from the Planck 2018 measurements in combination with Baryon Acoustic Oscillation (BAO) data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) DR2 (2024). From the results, we found that the discrepancies in \(H_0\) measurements are \(1.90\sigma\) and \(1.72\sigma\) between the Planck 2018 value \((H_0 = 67.4\pm0.5\ \mathrm{km,s^{-1},Mpc^{-1}})\) and our diffusive model values, \(H_0 = 67.27^{+0.54}_{-0.55}\;,\) and \(68.35^{+0.31}_{-0.29} \), respectively. We also observe that the effects of the interaction on cosmic evolution and structure formation; we emphasize this by computing the scale-dependent density contrast and the matter power spectrum, compared with the $\Lambda$CDM model.

arxiv.org/abs/2603.06838.title: On the relation between magnetic field strength and gas density in the interstellar medium. II. Density uncertainties and diffuse gas constraints
arxiv.org/abs/2603.06838.excerpt:
arXiv:2603.06838v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The relationship between magnetic field strength and gas density is essential to understand the interstellar medium and star formation. Zeeman measurements in dense atomic and molecular gas phases have traditionally been used to directly probe magnetic field strengths in the Milky Way. This allowed derivation of a relationship between magnetic field strength $B$ and gas number density $n$. We recently generalized this relation as a two-part power-law with non-zero slopes and a transition density given as $B/B_0 \propto (n/n_0)^{\alpha_1}$ for $n \le n_0$ and $(n/n_0)^{\alpha_2}$ for $n > n_0$. Here, we extend our previous hierarchical Bayesian framework by incorporating a large body of pulsar observations that probe the diffuse interstellar medium and explicitly modelling density uncertainties through a log-density intrinsic scatter $R_n$ applied to all densities. We also account for magnetic field geometry and measurement uncertainties through a magnetic hyperparameter to estimate $B$. This results in a stronger constraint on the diffuse gas part of the $B$--$n$ relation. Our results confirm a non-zero exponent in the diffuse gas and a broad transition density with our best model and data set yielding maximum a posteriori results of $\alpha_1 = 0.20^{+0.01}_{-0.03}$, $\alpha_2 = 0.65^{+0.06}_{-0.07}$, $n_0 = 3330^{+270}_{-3220}\,\text{cm}^{-3}$, and $B_0 = 10.11^{+0.71}_{-5.97}\,\mu\text{G}$.

arxiv.org/abs/2603.07879.title: Symmetry-Protected Momentum Exchange between Dark Matter and Dark Energy
arxiv.org/abs/2603.07879.excerpt:
arXiv:2603.07879v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present a particle physics motivated realization of interacting dark energy in which a radiatively stable dark energy sector couples to weakly interacting massive particle dark matter through pure momentum exchange. The dark energy field arises as a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone Boson from a complex scalar singlet charged under a softly broken global $U(1)_S$, while dark matter is identified with an inert scalar doublet stabilized by a discrete $Z_4$ symmetry. This symmetry structure allows renormalizable dark matter-dark energy portal operators; however, requiring the dark energy field to emerge as a radiatively stable pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone Boson necessitates their absence, leaving derivative interactions as the leading coupling. As a result, energy transfer between the dark sectors is absent at the background level, while momentum exchange modifies the evolution of cosmological perturbations. We implement the resulting interacting dark energy model self-consistently in the Boltzmann code CLASS and study its impact on the growth of structure. We find that, despite sizeable momentum exchange, the suppression of the clustering amplitude $\sigma_8$ saturates above the level required to fully resolve current low-redshift tensions. Our results demonstrate that symmetry-protected, momentum-exchange-only dark sector interactions possess an intrinsic limit on structure suppression, providing a theoretically controlled benchmark for interacting dark energy scenarios.

arxiv.org/abs/2603.20445.title: An Enriched Methane D/H Ratio in the Interstellar Object 3I/ATLAS
arxiv.org/abs/2603.20445.excerpt:
arXiv:2603.20445v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Interstellar objects are interlopers from other planetary systems, and their volatile compositions provide a glimpse into planet formation around their host star. We present near-infrared spectra of the coma of interstellar object 3I/ATLAS measured with the James Webb Space Telescope. Our results demonstrate an unexpectedly high D/H = $(3.33\pm0.31)\%$ for methane and represent an exceedingly rare detection of deuterated organic molecules in an interstellar object. This D/H ratio exceeds any other value for methane measured in the solar system, and is a factor of $14\pm2$ higher than that measured in comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko by the Rosetta spacecraft, the only other comet for which CH$_3$D has been detected. Both 3I/ATLAS and 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko show a higher degree of methane dueteration compared to water, consistent with trends seen in other solar system bodies and the nearby interstellar medium, where deuteration in organics exceeds that of water by up to an order of magnitude. The D/H ratio in methane itself is observationally unconstrained in extrasolar sources to date, but the enriched ratio in 3I/ATLAS is similar to those measured in methanol and formaldehyde toward primitive environments. The elevated D/H ratio for methane in 3I/ATLAS is consistent with the hypothesis that its ices formed in a cold, low metallicity interstellar or protostellar environment under a high cosmic ray irradiation rate (Cordiner et al. 2026).

arxiv.org/abs/2603.28857.title: Numerical calculations of neutron star mountains supported by crustal lattice pressure
arxiv.org/abs/2603.28857.excerpt:
arXiv:2603.28857v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Gravitational waves may set the spin frequencies of neutron stars in low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs). One mechanism for facilitating such emission is the formation of a mass asymmetry - or `mountain' - supported by elastic strains driven by thermal gradients. Most studies have focused either on the origin of the elastic strains or the temperature asymmetry in isolation, and have not considered the entire formation process. In previous work, we showed that anisotropic heat transport in magnetised accreting neutron stars can source a significant temperature asymmetry, and made rough estimates that suggested temperature-induced perturbations in the pressure supplied by the crustal lattice may be competitive with the widely known model of temperature-induced capture-layer shifts. In this paper we carry out detailed calculations to properly explore this scenario. We self-consistently calculate the temperature asymmetries, the perturbations in crustal lattice pressure, and the mass asymmetries within a single framework. For the first time, we make use of the set of realistic equations of state from the Brussels-Montreal nuclear energy-density functionals BSk19, BSk20, and BSk21 which describe all regions of accreting neutron stars in a thermodynamically consistent, unified way. We find these mountains are too small to dictate the spin-equilibrium of LMXBs, and estimate the level of gravitational wave emission they produce.

arxiv.org/abs/2604.18136.title: Equation of State for warm Neutron Star outer crusts
arxiv.org/abs/2604.18136.excerpt:
arXiv:2604.18136v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We describe the equation of state (EoS) of a warm ion plasma as obtained by performing microscopic many-body simulations using Molecular Dynamics computational techniques. Using the cold one-component plasma (OCP) composition in the Neutron Star (NS) outer crust assumed in \cite{Murarka_2022} with a representative heavy nucleus for each density, we refine previous calculations. We include electron screening and modeling of ions as finite-size Gaussian distributions in the interaction potential, together with an efficient Ewald energy summation procedure. From this, the EoS relation $P(n_B,T)$ is obtained as a function of baryonic number density $n_B\in[7.48\times 10^{-10},2.09\times10^{-4}]$ $ \rm fm^{-3}$ and temperature $k_{B}T\in[1,5]$ MeV in the NS outer crust conditions. In order to improve the usability of our results we provide tabulated data values along with a neural network parametrization available in the Zenodo repository, see https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15348712. We find that even at moderate temperatures, thermal effects of ions are key in the higher density region closer to the inner crust, when described using a thermal effective parametrization based on the thermal adiabatic index $\Gamma_{th}$. We compare our results with other EoS in the literature performing a critical discussion.

arxiv.org/abs/2604.19746.title: Calibration-Induced Systematics in SALT3 Training and Their Impact on Dark Energy Constraints from Stage IV Supernova Surveys
arxiv.org/abs/2604.19746.excerpt:
arXiv:2604.19746v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: In the coming years, the Vera Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (Rubin-LSST) and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope's (Roman) High Latitude Time Domain Survey (HLTDS) are expected to discover more than a million Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia), several orders of magnitude more than current samples and with a tighter control on systematic uncertainties. One of the largest systematic uncertainties in cosmological analyses with SNe Ia is the accuracy of the spectrophotometric model for SNe Ia time series data, which depends on the photometric calibration of the surveys. To quantify the impact of this uncertainty, we analyze simulated Rubin-LSST and HLTDS data, perturb the photometric zero-points and filter mean wavelengths, and propagate these systematics to spectral model recovery, estimated distances, and dark energy Figure of merit (FoM) based on the $w_0 w_a$CDM model. Zero-point shifts of 5 mmag and filter mean wavelength shifts of 5 angstrom lead to a $\sim 50\%$ decrease in the FoM relative to a statistical-only case when calibration uncertainties are propagated only through light-curve fitting. The same calibration shifts applied only during model training produce a smaller $\sim 13\%$ degradation. Contrary to previous analyses, calibration uncertainties in light-curve fitting dominate over those from model training. Their effect during light-curve fitting varies smoothly with redshift and is nearly degenerate with cosmology, preventing mitigation through self-calibration. Finally, we show that the FoM dependence on the size of the calibration uncertainties (in the range of expected sizes) is roughly linear.

arxiv.org/abs/2604.26072.title: Cosmic-web Environmental Impacts on the Halo Substructure Boosts to Dark Matter Annihilation Signals
arxiv.org/abs/2604.26072.excerpt:
arXiv:2604.26072v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The annihilation of dark matter (DM) particles is expected to produce Standard Model particles, providing a potential indirect signature of DM. The clumpy substructure of DM haloes amplifies the expected annihilation signal, an effect commonly quantified by the subhalo boost factor. Standard semi-analytic models usually treat this boost as a universal function of host-halo mass, neglecting systematic variations induced by the large-scale environment. In this work, we extend this framework by incorporating the influence of the cosmic web on subhalo populations. Using simulation-calibrated, environment-dependent ratios for host-halo concentrations, the subhalo mass function, and internal-structure proxies of subhalos based on the $V_{\max}$--$R_{\max}$ relation, we compute environment-conditioned boost predictions for haloes residing in filaments, walls, and voids. Our main result is the boost factor at fixed host-halo mass, expressed relative to the cosmic-mean prediction, $B(M,\mathrm{env})/B_{\mathrm{CM}}(M)$. We find a clear environmental modulation: in the fiducial distance-dependent model, filament haloes show a mass-dependent transition from a $\sim 15\%$ suppression at the low-mass end to a modest enhancement of $\sim 12\%$ for massive hosts, wall haloes remain intermediate, while void haloes stay suppressed by roughly $30$--$33\%$ across the explored host-mass range. These results should be interpreted as deterministic model predictions obtained by propagating environment-dependent ingredient ratios through two standard semi-analytic boost frameworks. We provide an environment-aware prescription for subhalo boosts, together with modular environmental corrections that may also be useful in indirect-detection forecasts, strong-lensing mass modeling, and related halo-population applications.

arxiv.org/abs/2605.21574.title: (LRDs)$^2$: The Low-ReDshift Little Red Dots Survey. II. DESI DR1 Sample
arxiv.org/abs/2605.21574.excerpt:
arXiv:2605.21574v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: JWST has revealed a substantial population of "Little Red Dots" (LRDs) at $z>4$, challenging conventional AGN frameworks. However, the low-redshift regime remains largely unexplored. In the second paper of the (LRDs)$^2$ series, we present a systematic selection from DESI DR1 and identify 27 LRDs at $z=0.2-0.9$, yielding a number density lower limit of $7.5\times10^{-10}$ cMpc$^{-3}$. We conducted near-IR spectroscopic follow-up observations for 21 of them, revealing their full SED shapes and emission lines. These low-$z$ LRDs share the hallmark properties of their high-$z$ counterparts: compact morphology, V-shaped UV-optical continua, broad Balmer emission with extreme decrements (median H$\alpha$/H$\beta\sim15$), frequent Balmer absorption (70%), and blackbody-like optical-to-near-IR continua. All have low metallicity, occupy the same regions in the BPT diagram as high-$z$ LRDs, and have softer ionizing spectra than typical AGNs. The consistency between low-$z$ and high-$z$ LRD properties indicates the same physical processes at work. The correlation between broad-line Balmer luminosity and $L_{5100}$ deviates from that of local type-1 AGNs, limiting the direct application of local BH mass calibrations. Ionized [O III] outflows are ubiquitous (78%). One LRD at $z=0.196$, J1717+3807, shows robust long-term variability in $i$ and WISE bands. The optical-to-NIR continua of LRDs reveal a wide range of temperatures $\sim2000-4700$ K (peak $0.6-1.4$ $\mu$m), with a subset showing cooler and larger envelopes than those at high $z$. Low-$z$ LRDs serve not only as proximate laboratories for probing the nature of LRDs, but also trace the cosmic evolution of this population from the cosmic dawn to the present day.

arxiv.org/abs/2605.23307.title: Superrotation and Jet Migration in Simulations of Giant Planet Atmospheres
arxiv.org/abs/2605.23307.excerpt:
arXiv:2605.23307v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The mean zonal flow on both Jupiter and Saturn consists of an intricate pattern of jets moving prograde or retrograde compared to the bulk planetary rotation. The strongest jet straddles the equator and is prograde, or superrotating. It is flanked by multiple retrograde/prograde pairs of weaker jets at high latitudes. Two candidate drivers of these jets are "shallow" quasi-two dimensional turbulence in the outermost stably stratified weather layer (WL) and "deep" buoyantly-driven Busse columns in the underlying convective zone (CZ). To study the respective roles of the WL and CZ, we implement two rotating, three-dimensional, anelastic convection simulations of a giant planet. In one case, the CZ is isolated, whereas in the other case, the upflows overshoot into a stably stratified near-surface layer, driving turbulence there. We regard this layer as a simplified WL, although we include the effects of stable stratification only, neglecting solar irradiation. In each case, we find that homogenization of an appropriately defined potential vorticity initially creates multiple jets at high latitudes, whereas Busse columns in the CZ drive equatorial superrotation. The presence of a simplified WL significantly alters the thermal wind balance, resulting in large deviations of the contours of the zonal flow from alignment with the rotation axis. Finally, the weaker high-latitude jets slowly migrate poleward and/or merge on a very long time scale (O(10) diffusion time scales or thousands of eddy turnover times).

arxiv.org/abs/2606.03776.title: Targeting black holes from metal-poor progenitors with next-generation gravitational-wave detectors
arxiv.org/abs/2606.03776.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.03776v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Next-generation gravitational-wave detectors such as the Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer will be able to detect binary black-hole mergers out to the cosmic dawn. Mergers observed in the local Universe represent a mixture of systems formed across the entire cosmic history, spanning a wide range of astrophysical environments. Iron-group elements govern metallicity effects on stellar evolution, making metallicity a key tracer that leaves a strong imprint on the black-hole population. We introduce the concept of a ``target'' redshift, $z_t$, defined as the epoch at which more than $90\%$ of stars form with metallicity $Z < 0.1\,Z_\odot$. This provides a straightforward way to isolate mergers originating from metal-poor environments. The determination of $z_t$ relies on the reconstruction of the cosmic star formation rate density as a function of iron abundance. This reconstruction is not unique, as it depends on the combination of different empirical scaling relations. Consequently, $z_t$ spans a broad range, from $z_t \sim 4$ to $z_t > 10$, depending on the adopted model variation. We present a statistical framework that enables rapid tests of astrophysical predictions against forecasted observations from next-generation \acrlong{gw} detectors. By quantifying variations in the binary black-hole merger-rate density between the target redshift and the local Universe, our approach maps evolutionary trends across parameter space and estimates the detection statistics required to distinguish genuine astrophysical variations from statistical fluctuations.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.20794.title: Constraints on Horndeski gravity with phantom crossing
arxiv.org/abs/2606.20794.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.20794v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Gravity models in which the dark energy equation of state crosses $w=-1$, also known as the phantom divide, have received extensive interest due to recent analyses favouring this behaviour. We introduce a new subclass of Horndeski scalar-tensor models capable of generating phantom crossing, whilst remaining minimally coupled to matter: the Asymptotic Cubic Galileon (ACG) models. We show that ACG models can jointly fit the expansion history inferred from observations of the Planck cosmic microwave background, baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument, and distance-ladder supernovae measurements from the Dark Energy Survey. We then demonstrate that requiring a positive galaxy-ISW cross-correlation, together with physically viable screening behaviour, substantially restricts the viable ACG parameter space. Model comparison metrics, including $\chi^{2}$ and Bayesian evidence, favour both ACG and $w_{0}w_{a}$CDM models over $\Lambda$CDM, with ACG providing a fit of comparable quality to $w_{0}w_{a}$CDM. Crucially, ACG models ground the observationally preferred $w_{0}w_{a}$CDM behaviour in a robust Lagrangian formulation. This enables interpretation beyond mere phenomenological fits, and motivates further tests of these models on nonlinear scales.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.23156.title: On the assessment of the disk truncation and detection of type-II-like bursts from the accreting millisecond X-ray Pulsar IGR J17062-6143
arxiv.org/abs/2606.23156.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.23156v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present a spectral analysis of the NuSTAR and NICER observations of the accreting millisecond X-ray pulsar IGR J17062-6143, performed in 2022. The source remained in the hard spectral state during these observations, with a luminosity of about $\sim$0.13-0.14 percent of the Eddington luminosity. The continuum emission of the NuSTAR spectrum is entirely dominated by a power-law component or by Comptonized emission of disc photons by a plasma with a high electron temperature ($\gtrsim100$ keV). The NuSTAR spectrum also reveals clear evidence of disc reflection, a broad Fe K line around 6-8 keV, and a Compton hump peaking at 20 keV, irrespective of the choice of the continuum models. Our spectral studies suggest a disk extending close to the neutron star surface ($\sim$6-20 $R_{\rm g}$) at low inclination angle ($\sim41$ degrees), as revealed by the self-consistent relativistic reflection model, relxill. In addition, we detected type-II-like bursts for the first time in the NICER observation of this source. Light curve profiles of type-II-like bursts exhibit different patterns, mostly associated with the so-called mode-0 and transition from mode-0 to mode-1 type-II bursts. The energy spectra of the persistent (pre-burst) and burst emission are well described by an absorbed Comptonization component, scattering disk- and blackbody-distributed photons, respectively, by a corona with a temperature of 1-3 keV. Although the origin of the type-II-like burst is not very clear, it has been possibly linked to disk-magnetosphere interaction of the accretion flow.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.24142.title: CHEX-MATE: AMALGAM weak-lensing analysis of 41 Planck Sunyaev-Zel'dovich-selected galaxy clusters
arxiv.org/abs/2606.24142.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.24142v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present a weak-lensing shear analysis of 41 Planck SZ-selected galaxy clusters at $0.11\le z\le 0.55$ from the CHEX-MATE sample, using wide-field Subaru/Suprime-Cam and CFHT/MegaPrime imaging from the AMALGAM project. We detect the azimuthally averaged weak-lensing signal around the X-ray peak of each cluster, achieving a median S/N of 6.5 per cluster. The $45^\circ$-rotated component has a median S/N of -0.1 and ranges from -1.8 to +1.8, consistent with zero. We model the excess surface mass density profile of each cluster with an NFW profile to infer weak-lensing mass and concentration constraints. The total systematic uncertainty in the weak-lensing mass calibration is assessed to be $8\%$. Using a hierarchical Bayesian framework, we then derive weak-lensing-calibrated scaling relations for the halo concentration, $c_{200}$, as a function of $M_{200}$ and redshift, and for the Planck SZ mass proxy, $M_{SZ}$, as a function of $M_{500}$ and redshift, while accounting for sample selection effects, weak-lensing modelling biases, and residual calibration uncertainty. At $M_{200}=10^{15}M_\odot$ and $z=0.25$, we find $c_{200}=3.53\pm0.71$ with an intrinsic scatter of $0.22\pm0.04$ dex. The inferred normalisation and scatter are consistent with recent $\Lambda$CDM predictions for massive haloes, with no significant mass or redshift dependence over the probed range. For the Planck mass proxy, our baseline regression yields $M_{SZ}/M_{500}=0.83\pm0.09$ at $M_{500}=7\times10^{14}M_\odot$ and $z=0.25$, with an intrinsic scatter of $0.10\pm0.02$ dex. A restricted model with fixed unit mass slope and no redshift evolution gives $1-b=0.72\pm0.11$. We also provide weak-lensing-calibrated posterior estimates of $M_{500}$ for the sample based on the baseline $M_{SZ}$--$M_{500}$--$z$ relation. These results provide an initial weak-lensing mass calibration for CHEX-MATE multi-probe cluster studies.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.29138.title: A Covariance-Aware Framework for Spatially Resolved Exoplanet Biosignature Inference with the Solar Gravitational Lens
arxiv.org/abs/2606.29138.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.29138v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Assessing possible life on an exoplanet requires spatial, spectral, temporal, and environmental context. We develop a covariance-aware Solar Gravitational Lens (SGL) framework for regional biosignature inference from reconstructed Einstein-ring measurements. A controlled 0.45-2.40 um Stokes-$I$ experiment uses ten illuminated cells, 128 channels, and R=70 to compare resolved and exactly projected disk spectra with common parameters and priors. Across 96 synthetic scenes, the joint gas, vegetation, and mineral block gains (1.52+/-0.03) nats after marginalizing cloud and calibration/response parameters; adding independently trained surrogate-discrepancy covariance gives (1.49+/-0.03) nats. Held-out mismatch nevertheless produces linearized shifts up to 6.08 posterior standard deviations; preserved precision does not establish unbiased recovery or evidence for life. For fixed Gaussian hypotheses, the expected log-likelihood-ratio loss under disk integration equals half the squared whitened contrast discarded by the projection. A separate 0.40-20 um continuum calculation provides absolute photon rates and observing-time estimates for an Earth-radius planet at 30 pc, observed from 650 AU. It includes source-averaged SGL amplification, finite-aperture extraction, coronal and host-star photons, detector noise, and a declared calibration floor. A reconstruction-covariance bracket reduces an 8 x 8 coadd gain from 7.77 to 3.00, costing 6.7 times the exposure in the statistical-noise limit. The framework connects regional spectroscopy and co-location tests to the physical and instrumental validation needed to assess exoplanet biospheres and possible biological activity.

arxiv.org/abs/2606.30742.title: ALMA visits the QSO MUSEUM: Connecting molecular gas and the cool circumgalactic medium around 37 $z\sim3$ quasars
arxiv.org/abs/2606.30742.excerpt:
arXiv:2606.30742v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Extended Ly$\alpha$ emission is ubiquitous around quasars and traces the cool circumgalactic medium, providing insights into halo gas dynamics and active galactic nucleus feedback. However, its connection to the cold molecular gas of the host galaxies remains largely unexplored. We characterize the molecular gas reservoirs of quasars at $z\sim3$ and investigate their connection to extended Ly$\alpha$ emission using ALMA CO(4-3) observations of 37 quasars from the QSO MUSEUM survey, previously mapped in Ly$\alpha$ with VLT/MUSE. We derive molecular gas masses and gas fractions, explore correlations with Ly$\alpha$ nebula and quasar properties, and search for CO-emitting companions. We detect 21/37 quasars in CO(4-3), with gas masses of $M_\mathrm{gas}\approx(3-40) \times10^9\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$. Quasars with the most massive molecular gas reservoirs are associated with the centrally dimmest Ly$\alpha$ nebulae, while those hosting the centrally brightest Ly$\alpha$ nebulae are generally not detected in CO. This suggests that gas and dust in the hosts regulate Ly$\alpha$ escape and consequently affect the emission from halo gas. We find evidence that lower-Eddington-ratio quasars harbor more massive gas reservoirs, while strongly accreting quasars ($\lambda_\mathrm{Edd} \gtrapprox 0.9$) likely deplete their gas; for example, through powerful quasar-driven outflows. Despite their higher molecular gas masses within the sample, CO-detected low-Eddington quasars exhibit low gas fractions with a median $M_\mathrm{gas}/M_* \sim 0.10$, below what is typically found for inactive star-forming galaxies. Six quasars are marginally resolved in CO, with effective radii up to $\sim 8\,\mathrm{kpc}$. In addition, we detect 14 high-fidelity companion galaxies, indicating overdense quasar environments with a quasar-galaxy cross-correlation length of $9.81^{+2.22}_{-2.05}\,h^{-1}\mathrm{cMpc}$.

arxiv.org/abs/2607.01005.title: Strong Lensing Tomography: Double and pseudo multi-source plane strong gravitational lensing to constrain dark energy
arxiv.org/abs/2607.01005.excerpt:
arXiv:2607.01005v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Tomographic measurements of gravitational lensing with different lens and source redshift distributions contain crucial information about the universe's relative expansion rate, and hence dark energy. While this technique is well-established in weak lensing, its application to strong lensing has traditionally focused on Double Source Plane Lenses (DSPLs). However, DSPLs are exceedingly rare and fundamentally limited by the Mass-Sheet Degeneracy (MSD), a systematic uncertainty underexplored in previous literature. To overcome these challenges, we introduce Pseudo Double-Source Plane Lenses (PDSPLs): pairs of independent single-source plane lenses with self-similar deflectors. This generalizes the DSPL formalism to the $\sim 10^5$ galaxy-galaxy lenses expected from LSST, Euclid, and Roman. Unlike true DSPLs, PDSPLs are free from the intermediate source mass problem by construction, eliminating the associated secondary MSD and the need for multi-plane ray tracing. We incorporate the deflector MSD into a hierarchical population model to forecast dark energy constraints in Flat $w_0w_a$CDM, showing that MSD severely degrades constraints from small DSPL samples and motivates our PDSPL statistical approach.
